sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

A tiny in-memory key-value store served over HTTP, written in TypeScript and run
directly by Node (>= 22, which executes `.ts` files natively).

**Constraint: no npm dependencies.** Only the Node standard library and local
imports are used. If a feature seems to need a package, use a stdlib equivalent

npm start            # listens on :8090 (override with PORT)

```sh
npm test             # node --test

| Method | Path     | Success | Errors |
|--------|----------|---------|--------|
| GET    | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"key", "value"}` | `404` key not found |
| PUT    | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` (raw body is the value, max 64 KiB) | `413` value too large |
| DELETE | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` | `404` key not found |

All error responses use the envelope:

```json
{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}
```

`method_not_allowed` (405).

## Goal
Build a small in-memory key-value store served over HTTP in TypeScript (using `node:http`), with:
- GET/PUT/DELETE on `/kv/:key`
- Standardized error envelope
- 64 KiB value size limit
- No npm dependencies (stdlib only)
- Tests via `node --test`
- **TTL support**: `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>`, expired keys behave as missing, injectable clock for tests

## Constraints & Preferences
- **No npm dependencies** — only Node standard library and local imports (stated as a rule by the user)
- TypeScript files run directly by Node ≥ 22 (actually v26.8.2 in this environment)
- `localhost` does NOT resolve in this environment (DNS `EAI_AGAIN`) — use `127.0.0.1` in tests
- Error responses must use the envelope: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`
- Values limited to 64 KiB; larger PUTs get 413
- Clock must be injectable so tests advance time without sleeping

## Progress
### Done
- [x] `git init` + project scaffold
- [x] `package.json` with `"type": "module"`, test script `node --test`, start script `node src/server.ts`
- [x] `src/store.ts` — in-memory `Map<string, string>` behind `set`, `get`, `del`
- [x] `src/server.ts` — `node:http` server with GET/PUT/DELETE on `/kv/:key`, exports `handler` for testability, main-module guard via `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`
- [x] `test/store.test.ts` — 5 unit tests (set/get/del behavior)
- [x] `test/server.test.ts` — 7 integration tests (random-port server, fetch-based, error body assertions)
- [x] Default port set to 8090
- [x] Error envelope standardized: `not_found` (404), `key_not_found` (404), `method_not_allowed` (405), `value_too_large` (413)
- [x] 64 KiB value limit enforced via `Buffer.byteLength` check in PUT branch
- [x] Boundary test: exactly 64 KiB accepted, 64 KiB + 1 byte rejected
- [x] `README.md` documenting constraint, API, run/test instructions
- [x] All 12 tests pass
- [x] 5 commits in git history
- [x] **TTL feature**: `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>` with validation (positive finite number, else `400 invalid_ttl`)
- [x] **Lazy expiry**: `get()` purges expired entries and returns `undefined`; `del()` returns `false` for expired keys
- [x] **Injectable clock**: `createStore(clock: Clock = () => Date.now())` factory; `KVStore` interface exported
- [x] **`createHandler(store: KVStore)`** factory in server.ts (replaces direct `handler` export)
- [x] **7 new TTL tests** (4 store-level with fake clock, 3 server-level with controllable `now` variable)
- [x] All 19 tests pass

## Key Decisions
- **`fileURLToPath` for main-module check**: `pathToFileURL(import.meta.url)` was wrong (it treats the URL as a path string, producing mangled paths like `/work/ts-kv/file:/...`). `fileURLToPath` is the correct function to convert a file URL to a filesystem path.
- **`127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` in tests**: `localhost` doesn't resolve via DNS in this environment (`EAI_AGAIN`).
- **`handler` exported from server.ts**: Allows tests to create their own server on a random port (`listen(0)`) without the main-module guard triggering.
- **`Buffer.byteLength` for size check**: 64 KiB means bytes, not characters; using byte-length avoids UTF-16 code unit confusion.
- **Post-read size check (not streaming)**: Full body is buffered before the check. Acceptable for a small in-memory store; a streaming cap could be added if needed.
- **`error()` helper function**: Wraps `json()` to produce the standard `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` envelope.
- **`createStore(clock)` factory pattern**: Chosen over a mutable `setClock()` for cleaner isolation — each test file gets its own store with its own clock. `node --test` runs each file in a separate process so no cross-contamination.
- **`createHandler(store)` factory**: Mirrors the store factory; server tests build their own handler on a store with a controllable fake clock, enabling TTL-over-HTTP tests without sleeping.
- **Lazy expiry (purge-on-read)**: No background sweeper; `get()` and `del()` check `clock() >= expiresAt` and delete the entry on the spot. Simple, no extra resources.
- **Expiry boundary uses `>=`**: A key set at time `T` with TTL `S` is expired at exactly `T + S*1000` ms (inclusive boundary).
- **`del()` returns `false` for expired keys**: Semantics — "expired keys behave as if they don't exist" — so `DELETE` on an expired key returns 404, same as a missing key.
- **Default named exports preserved**: `export const { get, set, del } = defaultStore` keeps backward compatibility with `store.test.ts`'s existing imports.

summary:
## Goal
Build a small in-memory key-value store served over HTTP in TypeScript (using `node:http`), with:
- GET/PUT/DELETE on `/kv/:key`
- Standardized error envelope
- 64 KiB value size limit
- No npm dependencies (stdlib only)
- Tests via `node --test`
- **TTL support**: `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>`, expired keys behave as missing, injectable clock for tests
- **Key listing**: `GET /kv` returns sorted live keys; optional `?prefix=` filter
- **Explicit port configuration**: port read from `KV_PORT` env var; fail at startup if missing or invalid

## Constraints & Preferences
- **No npm dependencies** — only Node standard library and local imports (stated as a rule by the user)
- TypeScript files run directly by Node ≥ 22 (actually v26.8.2 in this environment)
- `localhost` does NOT resolve in this environment (DNS `EAI_AGAIN`) — use `127.0.0.1` in tests
- Error responses must use the envelope: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`
- Values limited to 64 KiB; larger PUTs get 413
- Clock must be injectable so tests advance time without sleeping
- **No hard-coded port** — the port must come solely from `KV_PORT`; no default, no magic number in code or docs

## Progress
### Done
- [x] `git init` + project scaffold
- [x] `package.json` with `"type": "module"`, test script `node --test`, start script `node src/server.ts`
- [x] `src/store.ts` — in-memory `Map<string, string>` behind `set`, `get`, `del`, `list`
- [x] `src/server.ts` — `node:http` server with GET/PUT/DELETE on `/kv/:key`, GET on `/kv` (listing), exports `createHandler` for testability, main-module guard via `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`
- [x] `test/store.test.ts` — 9 unit tests (5 original + 4 TTL)
- [x] `test/server.test.ts` — 13 integration tests (7 original + 3 TTL + 3 listing)
- [x] `test/startup.test.ts` — 4 tests (KV_PORT missing, empty, invalid, valid)
- [x] Error envelope standardized: `not_found` (404), `key_not_found` (404), `method_not_allowed` (405), `value_too_large` (413), `invalid_ttl` (400)
- [x] 64 KiB value limit enforced via `Buffer.byteLength` check in PUT branch
- [x] Boundary test: exactly 64 KiB accepted, 64 KiB + 1 byte rejected
- [x] `README.md` documenting constraint, API, run/test instructions
- [x] All 12 initial tests pass
- [x] **TTL feature**: `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>` with validation (positive finite number, else `400 invalid_ttl`)
- [x] **Lazy expiry**: `get()` purges expired entries and returns `undefined`; `del()` returns `false` for expired keys
- [x] **Injectable clock**: `createStore(clock: Clock = () => Date.now())` factory; `KVStore` interface exported
- [x] **`createHandler(store: KVStore)`** factory in server.ts
- [x] **7 TTL tests** (4 store-level with fake clock, 3 server-level with controllable `now` variable)
- [x] All 19 tests pass (post-TTL)
- [x] Live smoke test: 2-second TTL confirmed end-to-end
- [x] README updated with `ttl` param, `invalid_ttl` code, TTL section
- [x] Committed as `0f7f117`
- [x] **`GET /kv` key listing**: `list(prefix?)` method on store; exact `/kv` route in server (before per-key regex); non-GET on `/kv` → 405
- [x] **6 listing tests** (3 store: sorted, prefix filter, expired purge; 3 server: listing+prefix, TTL expiry omission, 405 on non-GET)
- [x] All 25 tests pass (post-listing)
- [x] Live smoke test: sorted listing, prefix filter, 405 on PUT /kv
- [x] README table updated with `GET /kv` row
- [x] Committed as `ae05b58`
- [x] **`KV_PORT` env var**: port read solely from `KV_PORT`; missing/empty → clear error + exit 1; non-integer or out of 1–65535 range → clear error + exit 1
- [x] **No hard-coded port**: `8090` removed from repo entirely (grep-verified); README uses `<port>` placeholder
- [x] **4 startup tests** in `test/startup.test.ts`: missing, empty, invalid `KV_PORT` all exit 1 with message; valid `KV_PORT` starts server that answers `GET /kv`

- [x] Committed as `e9dcd04`

### In Progress
- (none — all requested work is complete)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Key Decisions
- **`fileURLToPath` for main-module check**: `pathToFileURL(import.meta.url)` was wrong. `fileURLToPath` is correct for converting a file URL to a filesystem path.
- **`127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` in tests**: `localhost` doesn't resolve via DNS in this environment (`EAI_AGAIN`).
- **`createHandler(store)` factory**: Allows tests to create their own server on a random port (`listen(0)`) without the main-module guard triggering.
- **`Buffer.byteLength` for size check**: 64 KiB means bytes, not characters.
- **Post-read size check (not streaming)**: Full body is buffered before the check. Acceptable for a small in-memory store.
- **`error()` helper function**: Wraps `json()` to produce the standard `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` envelope.
- **`createStore(clock)` factory pattern**: Chosen over a mutable `setClock()` for cleaner isolation. `node --test` runs each file in a separate process.
- **Lazy expiry (purge-on-read)**: No background sweeper; `get()` and `del()` check `clock() >= expiresAt` and delete on the spot.
- **Expiry boundary uses `>=`**: A key set at time `T` with TTL `S` is expired at exactly `T + S*1000` ms.
- **`del()` returns `false` for expired keys**: "Expired keys behave as if they don't exist."
- **`list()` also purges expired entries**: Consistent with `get()`/`del()` — iterating and lazily removing expired keys before filtering.
- **Exact `/kv` route before per-key regex**: Prevents the regex `^\/kv\/([^/]+)$` from accidentally matching (it wouldn't, but explicit ordering is clearer and allows 405 semantics specific to the listing endpoint).
- **`KV_PORT` validated at startup only in main-module block**: The check is inside the `process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` guard, so test imports of `createHandler` are unaffected.
- **`KV_PORT` validation covers empty string**: `rawPort === undefined || rawPort === ""` treats both as "missing."
- **`Number()` + `Number.isInteger()` for port validation**: Handles non-numeric strings, floats, out-of-range values. `Number(" 8090 ")` trims whitespace (acceptable).
- **`<port>` placeholder in README and error message**: Avoids introducing any specific number that could be mistaken for a default.
- **Startup tests spawn `node src/server.ts` as child process**: Uses `execFile(process.execPath, [serverPath], { env })` to control the environment precisely. The "valid" test waits for the "listening" stdout line before fetching to avoid race conditions.
- **Fixed port 18901 in startup test**: Chosen as an unlikely-to-collide high port; acceptable for a test that kills its child in `finally`.

## Next Steps
1. (none required — all user requests fulfilled and committed)
2. If user requests more features: maintain stdlib-only constraint, use the `error()` helper for any new error paths, add tests to `test/server.test.ts` or `test/store.test.ts`
3. Any future smoke/live tests should use a fresh port (check with `ss -ltnp`) to avoid `EADDRINUSE` from stale processes

## Critical Context
- **Working directory**: `/work/ts-kv`
- **Node version**: v26.8.2
- **File structure**:
  ```
  ts-kv/
  ├── package.json
  ├── README.md
  ├── src/
  │   ├── store.ts        # createStore(clock) factory, KVStore interface (set, get, del, list), Clock type, defaultStore + named exports
  │   └── server.ts       # createHandler(store) factory, main-module guard with KV_PORT validation
  └── test/
      ├── store.test.ts   # 12 tests (5 original + 4 TTL + 3 listing)
      ├── server.test.ts  # 13 tests (7 original + 3 TTL + 3 listing)
      └── startup.test.ts # 4 tests (KV_PORT missing/empty/invalid/valid)
  ```
- **Error codes used**: `not_found`, `key_not_found`, `value_too_large`, `method_not_allowed`, `invalid_ttl`
- **Stale server pitfall**: Ports can be left bound by previous runs; always check `ss -ltnp` and kill stale processes before live-testing. `pkill -f "node src/server.ts"` can match the shell's own command line — use precise PID kill or `ss` to identify.
- **Git commits** (oldest to newest): `29f4d1a`, `89c638c`, `61a8f54`, `81e912c`, `df02978`, `0f7f117`, `ae05b58`, `e9dcd04`
- **Store API**: `createStore(clock?)` → `{ set(key, value, ttlSeconds?), get(key), del(key), list(prefix?) }`; `Entry = { value: string, expiresAt: number | null }`
- **Server API**: `createHandler(store: KVStore)` → `(req, res) => Promise<void>`; main block validates `KV_PORT` then does `createServer(createHandler(createStore())).listen(port)`
- **TTL validation in handler**: `url.searchParams.get("ttl")` → if present, `Number(ttl)` must be finite and > 0, else `400 invalid_ttl`
- **Test clock pattern**: `let now = 0; const store = createStore(() => now);` — tests advance `now` to simulate time passing
- **`KV_PORT` startup messages**:
  - Missing/empty: `Missing required environment variable KV_PORT.\nStart the server with KV_PORT set to the port to listen on, e.g.:\n  KV_PORT=<port> node src/server.ts`
  - Invalid: `Invalid KV_PORT "…": must be an integer between 1 and 65535.`

# ts-kv A tiny in-memory key-value store served over HTTP, written in TypeScript and run directly by Node (>= 22, which executes `.ts` files natively). **Constraint: no npm dependencies.** Only the Node standard library and local imports are used. If a feature seems to need a package, use a stdlib equivalent or hand-roll it. ## Run The port is taken from the `KV_PORT` environment variable. The server exits at startup with an error if `KV_PORT` is missing or not a valid port. ```sh KV_PORT= npm start ``` ## Test ```sh npm test # node --test ``` ## API Base path `/kv/:key`, JSON responses. | Method | Path | Success | Errors | |--------|----------|---------|--------| | GET | `/kv?prefix=

` | `200 {"keys": [...]}` (sorted live keys; optional prefix filter) | `405` for non-GET | | GET | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"key", "value"}` | `404` key not found | | PUT | `/kv/:key?ttl=` | `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` (raw body is the value, max 64 KiB) | `400` invalid ttl, `413` value too large | | DELETE | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` | `404` key not found | All error responses use the envelope: ```json {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}} ``` Codes: `not_found` (unknown path), `key_not_found`, `value_too_large`, `method_not_allowed` (405), `invalid_ttl` (400). ### TTL `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=` stores the key with a time-to-live. The clock is injected into the store (`createStore(clock)`) so tests advance time without sleeping. Expired keys behave exactly as missing: `GET` and `DELETE` return `404 key_not_found`. `ttl` must be a positive number of seconds.

edits.newText:
### TTL

`PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>` stores the key with a time-to-live. The clock is
injected into the store (`createStore(clock)`) so tests advance time without
sleeping. Expired keys behave exactly as missing: `GET` and `DELETE` return
`404 key_not_found`. `ttl` must be a positive number of seconds.

## Persistence

When `KV_DATA_FILE` is set, the store is loaded from that JSON file on startup
and snapshotted back to it when the process receives `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`.
Without it, the store is purely in-memory.

- **First run:** if the file does not exist, the store starts empty (the file
  is created on the first shutdown snapshot; parent directories are created
  as needed).
- **Corrupt file:** a file that is not valid JSON or does not have the
  snapshot shape causes startup to fail with a clear error (exit 1).
- **Expired keys are not written:** the snapshot contains live entries only.
  Keys with a remaining TTL keep it, recorded as `ttlMs` relative to the
  snapshot time, so a restarted server preserves the original expiry.

Snapshot format:

```json
{
  "greeting": { "value": "hi", "ttlMs": null },
  "session:abc": { "value": "...", "ttlMs": 41250 }
}
```

content.text:
Persistence is in, all 39 tests green, committed as `8f9a6de`.

**How it works**
- **`src/store.ts`** — `serialize()` snapshots live entries as `{value, ttlMs}` (remaining TTL in ms; expired keys are purged and omitted). `load(data)` restores entries relative to the current clock.
- **`src/persist.ts`** (new) — `loadStore(file)` and `saveStore(store, file)`. Missing file = first run (empty store, parent dirs created); corrupt or wrong-shaped file = clear startup error.
- **`src/server.ts`** — `KV_DATA_FILE` is optional (unset = in-memory only, as before). On startup it loads the file (fail-fast with exit 1 if corrupt); on `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` it writes the snapshot, logs `store saved to …`, and exits 0 (exit 1 if the write fails).

**Format**
```json
{ "greeting": { "value": "hi", "ttlMs": null }, "session:abc": { "value": "…", "ttlMs": 41250 } }
```
Remaining-TTL (not absolute epoch) means a restart preserves the original expiry — and the fake-clock tests stay possible.

**Tests** (+10)
- Store: `serialize` omits expired + records remaining ttl, `load` re-anchors expiry to load-time clock, round-trip
- Persist: save/load units, missing file, invalid JSON, wrong shape — each with a clean temp dir
- E2e: spawn real server → PUT two keys (one TTL'd) → SIGTERM → assert exit 0 + snapshot contents → restart → both keys come back
- Shared `test/helpers.ts` (`spawnServer`/`waitForListening`/`waitForExit`) now used by both startup and persist tests

**Live-verified**: restart reloads `dur`, expired `short` (omitted from snapshot) 404s; corrupt file → `Failed to load data file: … not valid JSON …` + exit 1; first run with nested path creates dirs and writes `{}` on shutdown.

One test-design note: `loadStore` takes an optional `clock` (defaulting to the real one) so TTL semantics are testable without sleeping — same pattern as `createStore`.

summary:
## Goal
Build a small in-memory key-value store served over HTTP in TypeScript (using `node:http`), with:
- GET/PUT/DELETE on `/kv/:key`
- Standardized error envelope
- 64 KiB value size limit
- No npm dependencies (stdlib only)
- Tests via `node --test`
- **TTL support**: `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>`, expired keys behave as missing, injectable clock for tests
- **Key listing**: `GET /kv` returns sorted live keys; optional `?prefix=` filter
- **Explicit port configuration**: port read from `KV_PORT` env var; fail at startup if missing or invalid
- **Persistence**: on shutdown (SIGTERM/SIGINT), write store to JSON file specified by `KV_DATA_FILE`; load on startup; expired keys excluded

## Constraints & Preferences
- **No npm dependencies** — only Node standard library and local imports (stated as a rule by the user)
- TypeScript files run directly by Node ≥ 22 (actually v26.8.2 in this environment)
- `localhost` does NOT resolve in this environment (DNS `EAI_AGAIN`) — use `127.0.0.1` in tests
- Error responses must use the envelope: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`
- Values limited to 64 KiB; larger PUTs get 413
- Clock must be injectable so tests advance time without sleeping
- **No hard-coded port** — the port must come solely from `KV_PORT`; no default, no magic number in code or docs
- **`KV_DATA_FILE` is optional** — unset means in-memory only; no persistence

## Progress

- [x] `test/store.test.ts` — 15 unit tests (5 original + 4 TTL + 3 listing + 3 serialize/load)

## Key Decisions
- **`fileURLToPath` for main-module check**: `pathToFileURL(import.meta.url)` was wrong. `fileURLToPath` is correct for converting a file URL to a filesystem path.
- **`127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` in tests**: `localhost` doesn't resolve via DNS in this environment (`EAI_AGAIN`).
- **`createHandler(store)` factory**: Allows tests to create their own server on a random port (`listen(0)`) without the main-module guard triggering.
- **`Buffer.byteLength` for size check**: 64 KiB means bytes, not characters.
- **Post-read size check (not streaming)**: Full body is buffered before the check. Acceptable for a small in-memory store.
- **`error()` helper function**: Wraps `json()` to produce the standard `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` envelope.
- **`createStore(clock)` factory pattern**: Chosen over a mutable `setClock()` for cleaner isolation. `node --test` runs each file in a separate process.
- **Lazy expiry (purge-on-read)**: No background sweeper; `get()` and `del()` check `clock() >= expiresAt` and delete on the spot.
- **Expiry boundary uses `>=`**: A key set at time `T` with TTL `S` is expired at exactly `T + S*1000` ms.
- **`del()` returns `false` for expired keys**: "Expired keys behave as if they don't exist."
- **`list()` also purges expired entries**: Consistent with `get()`/`del()` — iterating and lazily removing expired keys before filtering.
- **Exact `/kv` route before per-key regex**: Prevents the regex `^\/kv\/([^/]+)$` from accidentally matching (it wouldn't, but explicit ordering is clearer and allows 405 semantics specific to the listing endpoint).
- **`KV_PORT` validated at startup only in main-module block**: The check is inside the `process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` guard, so test imports of `createHandler` are unaffected.
- **`KV_PORT` validation covers empty string**: `rawPort === undefined || rawPort === ""` treats both as "missing."
- **`Number()` + `Number.isInteger()` for port validation**: Handles non-numeric strings, floats, out-of-range values. `Number(" 8090 ")` trims whitespace (acceptable).
- **`<port>` placeholder in README and error message**: Avoids introducing any specific number that could be mistaken for a default.
- **Startup tests spawn `node src/server.ts` as child process**: Uses `execFile(process.execPath, [serverPath], { env })` to control the environment precisely. The "valid" test waits for the "listening" stdout line before fetching to avoid race conditions.
- **Fixed port 18901 in startup test**: Chosen as an unlikely-to-collide high port; acceptable for a test that kills its child in `finally`.
- **`KV_DATA_FILE` is optional**: Unset = in-memory only. Not required (unlike `KV_PORT`). Keeps the store library usable without a file.
- **Persist remaining TTL in ms (relative), not absolute epoch**: Works with injectable fake clock in tests. On load, `expiresAt = clock() + ttlMs`. Absolute epoch would not work with the test clock starting at 0.
- **`serialize()` purges expired entries as a side effect**: Iterates the map, deletes expired entries, builds output object. Consistent with lazy-expiry semantics of `get`/`list`.
- **`load()` replaces all contents**: `data.clear()` then re-insert. On startup the store is fresh so merge == replace, but replace is more predictable as an API.
- **Separate `src/persist.ts` module**: Clean layering — `store.ts` is pure in-memory + clock; `persist.ts` is file I/O + validation; `server.ts` is HTTP. `loadStore`/`saveStore` are testable independently.
- **Shape validation via `isPersistedStore` type guard**: Top-level must be a plain object; each entry must be `{ value: string, ttlMs: number | null }`. Catches hand-edited or corrupt files with a clear error message.
- **Missing file on load = first run (empty store)**: `ENOENT` is the only error code that yields a graceful empty store. Any other I/O error rethrows.
- **`loadStore(file, clock?)` has optional clock parameter**: Needed for tests that use a fake clock. Production uses the default `() => Date.now()`.
- **`mkdirSync(dirname(file), { recursive: true })` on both load and save**: Ensures parent directory exists. `dirname("kv.json")` = `"."` which is a no-op.
- **Shutdown is idempotent**: `shuttingDown` flag prevents double-save if both SIGINT and SIGTERM arrive.
- **Exit codes**: Save failure → `process.exit(1)` with clear message. Success → `process.exit(0)`.
- **No atomic write (temp file + rename)**: Acceptable for a small store; documented as last-known-good snapshot.

## Next Steps
1. Update `README.md` with a Persistence section: document `KV_DATA_FILE` (optional), snapshot format, first-run behavior, corrupt-file behavior, shutdown save
2. Commit the persistence feature
3. If user requests more: maintain stdlib-only constraint, add tests to appropriate test file

content.text:
Load test is in — `scripts/load.ts`, run with `npm run load` (or `node scripts/load.ts`).

**Design**
- **In-process server**: imports `createHandler`/`createStore` directly (no `KV_PORT` needed — the main-module guard doesn't apply to imports) and listens on `127.0.0.1:0` for an ephemeral port.
- **20,000 requests**: 10,000 PUTs, then 10,000 GETs (the GET phase runs after PUTs complete, so every GET is a guaranteed hit).
- **50 in flight**: a fixed pool of 50 async workers pulling sequential op indices off a shared cursor (`next++` is safe — no `await` between read and increment).
- **Realistic working set**: 1,000 keys, 128-byte values; each response body is drained so keep-alive sockets recycle.
- **Report**: wall time, total + per-phase throughput, error count by status, latency p50/p90/p99/max. Exits 1 if any request failed.
- **Clean shutdown**: `server.closeAllConnections()` + `close()`, so the process exits promptly instead of hanging on keep-alive sockets.

**Result on this machine**
```
requests   : 20000 (10000 PUT + 10000 GET)
wall time  : 1.461 s
throughput : 13686 req/s   (PUT phase 11072, GET phase 17916)
errors     : 0
latency ms : p50 3.15  p90 5.02  p99 7.74  max 138.19
```
The 138 ms max is first-burst socket warmup; the 99th percentile is well under 8 ms. Test suite still green (39/39).

# ts-kv A tiny in-memory key-value store served over HTTP, written in TypeScript and run directly by Node (>= 22, which executes `.ts` files natively). **Constraint: no npm dependencies.** Only the Node standard library and local imports are used. If a feature seems to need a package, use a stdlib equivalent or hand-roll it. ## Run The port is taken from the `KV_PORT` environment variable. The server exits at startup with an error if `KV_PORT` is missing or not a valid port. ```sh KV_PORT= npm start ``` Optionally set `KV_DATA_FILE` to persist the store to a JSON file (see [Persistence](#persistence)): ```sh KV_PORT= KV_DATA_FILE=data/kv.json npm start ``` ## Test ```sh npm test # node --test ``` ## API Base path `/kv/:key`, JSON responses. | Method | Path | Success | Errors | |--------|----------|---------|--------| | GET | `/kv?prefix=

` | `200 {"keys": [...]}` (sorted live keys; optional prefix filter) | `405` for non-GET | | GET | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"key", "value"}` | `404` key not found | | PUT | `/kv/:key?ttl=` | `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` (raw body is the value, max 64 KiB) | `400` invalid ttl, `413` value too large | | DELETE | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` | `404` key not found | All error responses use the envelope: ```json {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}} ``` Codes: `not_found` (unknown path), `key_not_found`, `value_too_large`, `method_not_allowed` (405), `invalid_ttl` (400). ### TTL `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=` stores the key with a time-to-live. The clock is injected into the store (`createStore(clock)`) so tests advance time without sleeping. Expired keys behave exactly as missing: `GET` and `DELETE` return `404 key_not_found`. `ttl` must be a positive number of seconds. ## Persistence When `KV_DATA_FILE` is set, the store is loaded from that JSON file on startup and snapshotted back to it when the process receives `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`. Without it, the store is purely in-memory. - **First run:** if the file does not exist, the store starts empty (the file is created on the first shutdown snapshot; parent directories are created as needed). - **Corrupt file:** a file that is not valid JSON or does not have the snapshot shape causes startup to fail with a clear error (exit 1). - **Expired keys are not written:** the snapshot contains live entries only. Keys with a remaining TTL keep it, recorded as `ttlMs` relative to the snapshot time, so a restarted server preserves the original expiry. Snapshot format: ```json { "greeting": { "value": "hi", "ttlMs": null }, "session:abc": { "value": "...", "ttlMs": 41250 } } ```

### TTL

`PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>` stores the key with a time-to-live. The clock is
injected into the store (`createStore(clock)`) so tests advance time without
sleeping. Expired keys behave exactly as missing: `GET` and `DELETE` return
`404 key_not_found`. `ttl` must be a positive number of seconds.

### ETags

`GET` and `PUT` responses carry an `ETag`: a strong tag — the quoted
SHA-256 hex digest of the value (RFC 7232). Send `If-None-Match` with a
previously returned tag and the server answers `304 Not Modified` with an
empty body instead of the value; the tag is still sent on the 304. Weak
(`W/`) tags, `*`, and comma-separated lists are all accepted (weak comparison).
The tag changes whenever the value changes, so a stale tag simply gets a full
`200` again.

Done — committed as `ec4127b`.

**Implementation** (`src/server.ts`)
- **`etagFor(value)`** — strong ETag per RFC 7232: quoted SHA-256 hex digest of the value. Sent on `GET 200` and `PUT 200`.
- **`If-None-Match` → `304`** — when any offered tag weakly matches the current tag, the response is an empty-body `304 Not Modified` that still carries the `ETag` header (as RFC 7232 §3.2 recommends). No body, no JSON.
- **`etagMatches()`** — proper weak comparison: accepts `W/"…"` weak forms, `*`, and comma-separated lists; a tag only matches the *current* value, so stale tags fall through to a full `200`.
- No store changes — the tag is derived from the value, so it stays correct across restarts (persistence stores values, not tags).

**Tests** (+5, 44/44 green)
- `etagMatches` unit: exact, weak, `*`, list, and non-matching forms
- ETag on GET/PUT equals an independently computed SHA-256
- Matching tag → 304, empty body, tag resent
- Stale tag → full 200
- Tag changes when the value changes

**Live-verified with curl**: `hello` → `etag: "2cf24dba…824"` (the actual SHA-256 of `hello`), conditional GET → `304` with empty body, stale tag → `200`. Load test still runs at ~13k req/s — hashing is negligible.

summary:
## Goal
Build a small in-memory key-value store served over HTTP in TypeScript (using `node:http`), with:
- GET/PUT/DELETE on `/kv/:key`
- Standardized error envelope
- 64 KiB value size limit
- No npm dependencies (stdlib only)
- Tests via `node --test`
- **TTL support**: `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>`, expired keys behave as missing, injectable clock for tests
- **Key listing**: `GET /kv` returns sorted live keys; optional `?prefix=` filter
- **Explicit port configuration**: port read from `KV_PORT` env var; fail at startup if missing or invalid
- **Persistence**: on shutdown (SIGTERM/SIGINT), write store to JSON file specified by `KV_DATA_FILE`; load on startup; expired keys excluded
- **Load test**: in-process benchmark script (`scripts/load.ts`) sending 20,000 requests with 50 in flight

## Constraints & Preferences
- **No npm dependencies** — only Node standard library and local imports (stated as a rule by the user)
- TypeScript files run directly by Node ≥ 22 (actually v26.8.2 in this environment)
- `localhost` does NOT resolve in this environment (DNS `EAI_AGAIN`) — use `127.0.0.1` in tests
- Error responses must use the envelope: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`
- Values limited to 64 KiB; larger PUTs get 413
- Clock must be injectable so tests advance time without sleeping
- **No hard-coded port** — the port must come solely from `KV_PORT`; no default, no magic number in code or docs
- **`KV_DATA_FILE` is optional** — unset means in-memory only; no persistence

## Key Decisions
- **`fileURLToPath` for main-module check**: `pathToFileURL(import.meta.url)` was wrong. `fileURLToPath` is correct for converting a file URL to a filesystem path.
- **`127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` in tests**: `localhost` doesn't resolve via DNS in this environment (`EAI_AGAIN`).
- **`createHandler(store)` factory**: Allows tests to create their own server on a random port (`listen(0)`) without the main-module guard triggering.
- **`Buffer.byteLength` for size check**: 64 KiB means bytes, not characters.
- **Post-read size check (not streaming)**: Full body is buffered before the check. Acceptable for a small in-memory store.
- **`error()` helper function**: Wraps `json()` to produce the standard `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` envelope.
- **`createStore(clock)` factory pattern**: Chosen over a mutable `setClock()` for cleaner isolation. `node --test` runs each file in a separate process.
- **Lazy expiry (purge-on-read)**: No background sweeper; `get()` and `del()` check `clock() >= expiresAt` and delete on the spot.
- **Expiry boundary uses `>=`**: A key set at time `T` with TTL `S` is expired at exactly `T + S*1000` ms.
- **`del()` returns `false` for expired keys**: "Expired keys behave as if they don't exist."
- **`list()` also purges expired entries**: Consistent with `get()`/`del()` — iterating and lazily removing expired keys before filtering.
- **Exact `/kv` route before per-key regex**: Prevents the regex from accidentally matching; explicit ordering allows 405 semantics specific to the listing endpoint.
- **`KV_PORT` validated at startup only in main-module block**: The check is inside the `process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` guard, so test imports of `createHandler` are unaffected.
- **`KV_PORT` validation covers empty string**: `rawPort === undefined || rawPort === ""` treats both as "missing."
- **`Number()` + `Number.isInteger()` for port validation**: Handles non-numeric strings, floats, out-of-range values.
- **`<port>` placeholder in README and error message**: Avoids introducing any specific number that could be mistaken for a default.
- **Startup tests spawn `node src/server.ts` as child process**: Uses `execFile(process.execPath, [serverPath], { env })` to control the environment precisely.
- **Fixed port 18901 in startup test**: Chosen as an unlikely-to-collide high port; acceptable for a test that kills its child in `finally`.
- **`KV_DATA_FILE` is optional**: Unset = in-memory only. Not required (unlike `KV_PORT`).

- **`serialize()` purges expired entries as a side effect**: Consistent with lazy-expiry semantics.
- **`load()` replaces all contents**: `data.clear()` then re-insert.
- **Separate `src/persist.ts` module**: Clean layering — `store.ts` is pure in-memory + clock; `persist.ts` is file I/O + validation; `server.ts` is HTTP.
- **Shape validation via `isPersistedStore` type guard**: Top-level must be a plain object; each entry must be `{ value: string, ttlMs: number | null }`.

- **`loadStore(file, clock?)` has optional clock parameter**: Needed for tests that use a fake clock.
- **`mkdirSync(dirname(file), { recursive: true })` on both load and save**: Ensures parent directory exists.

``` ## API Base path `/kv/:key`, JSON responses. | Method | Path | Success | Errors | |--------|----------|---------|--------| | GET | `/kv?prefix=

` | `200 {"keys": [...]}` (sorted live keys; optional prefix filter) | `405` for non-GET | | GET | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"key", "value"}` + `ETag` header; `304` (empty body, `ETag` header) when `If-None-Match` matches | `404` key not found | | PUT | `/kv/:key?ttl=` | `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` + `ETag` header (raw body is the value, max 64 KiB) | `400` invalid ttl, `412` If-Match failed, `413` value too large | | DELETE | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` | `404` key not found | All error responses use the envelope: ```json {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}} ``` Codes: `not_found` (unknown path), `key_not_found`, `value_too_large`, `method_not_allowed` (405), `invalid_ttl` (400), `precondition_failed` (412). ### TTL `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=` stores the key with a time-to-live. The clock is injected into the store (`createStore(clock)`) so tests advance time without sleeping. Expired keys behave exactly as missing: `GET` and `DELETE` return `404 key_not_found`. `ttl` must be a positive number of seconds. ### ETags `GET` and `PUT` responses carry an `ETag`: a strong tag — the quoted SHA-256 hex digest of the value (RFC 7232). Send `If-None-Match` with a previously returned tag and the server answers `304 Not Modified` with an empty body instead of the value; the tag is still sent on the 304. Weak (`W/`) tags, `*`, and comma-separated lists are all accepted (weak comparison). The tag changes whenever the value changes, so a stale tag simply gets a full `200` again. **Compare-and-set:** a `PUT` with an `If-Match` header is applied only if the current value's ETag matches (same weak-comparison rules: `W/` tags, `*`, comma-separated lists). On failure the store is unchanged and the response is `412` with the standard error envelope (`precondition_failed`). A missing key fails the precondition too, including for `If-Match: *` — so `If-Match: ` on a fresh key is the safe "create if absent with this base" form, and a failed write tells you to re-read and retry. ## Persistence When `KV_DATA_FILE` is set, the store is loaded from that JSON file on startup and snapshotted back to it when the process receives `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`. Without it, the store is purely in-memory. - **First run:** if the file does not exist, the store starts empty (the file is created on the first shutdown snapshot; parent directories are created as needed). - **Corrupt file:** a file that is not valid JSON or does not have the snapshot shape causes startup to fail with a clear error (exit 1). - **Expired keys are not written:** the snapshot contains live entries only. Keys with a remaining TTL keep it, recorded as `ttlMs` relative to the snapshot time, so a restarted server preserves the original expiry. Snapshot format: ```json { "greeting": { "value": "hi", "ttlMs": null }, "session:abc": { "value": "...", "ttlMs": 41250 } } ```

Build a small in-memory key-value store served over HTTP in TypeScript (using `node:http`), with:
- GET/PUT/DELETE on `/kv/:key`
- Standardized error envelope

## Key Decisions
- **`fileURLToPath` for main-module check**: `pathToFileURL(import.meta.url)` was wrong. `fileURLToPath` is correct for converting a file URL to a filesystem path.
- **`127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` in tests**: `localhost` doesn't resolve via DNS in this environment (`EAI_AGAIN`).
- **`createHandler(store)` factory**: Allows tests to create their own server on a random port (`listen(0)`) without the main-module guard triggering.
- **`Buffer.byteLength` for size check**: 64 KiB means bytes, not characters.
- **Post-read size check (not streaming)**: Full body is buffered before the check. Acceptable for a small in-memory store.
- **`error()` helper function**: Wraps `json()` to produce the standard `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` envelope.
- **`createStore(clock)` factory pattern**: Chosen over a mutable `setClock()` for cleaner isolation. `node --test` runs each file in a separate process.
- **Lazy expiry (purge-on-read)**: No background sweeper; `get()` and `del()` check `clock() >= expiresAt` and delete on the spot.
- **Expiry boundary uses `>=`**: A key set at time `T` with TTL `S` is expired at exactly `T + S*1000` ms.
- **`del()` returns `false` for expired keys**: "Expired keys behave as if they don't exist."
- **`list()` also purges expired entries**: Consistent with `get()`/`del()` — iterating and lazily removing expired keys before filtering.
- **Exact `/kv` route before per-key regex**: Prevents the regex from accidentally matching; explicit ordering allows 405 semantics specific to the listing endpoint.
- **`KV_PORT` validated at startup only in main-module block**: The check is inside the `process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` guard, so test imports of `createHandler` are unaffected.
- **`KV_PORT` validation covers empty string**: `rawPort === undefined || rawPort === ""` treats both as "missing."
- **`Number()` + `Number.isInteger()` for port validation**: Handles non-numeric strings, floats, out-of-range values.
- **`<port>` placeholder in README and error message**: Avoids introducing any specific number that could be mistaken for a default.
- **Startup tests spawn `node src/server.ts` as child process**: Uses `execFile(process.execPath, [serverPath], { env })` to control the environment precisely.
- **Fixed port 18901 in startup test**: Chosen as an unlikely-to-collide high port; acceptable for a test that kills its child in `finally`.
- **`KV_DATA_FILE` is optional**: Unset = in-memory only. Not required (unlike `KV_PORT`).
- **Persist remaining TTL in ms (relative), not absolute epoch**: Works with injectable fake clock in tests. On load, `expiresAt = clock() + ttlMs`.
- **`serialize()` purges expired entries as a side effect**: Consistent with lazy-expiry semantics.
- **`load()` replaces all contents**: `data.clear()` then re-insert.
- **Separate `src/persist.ts` module**: Clean layering — `store.ts` is pure in-memory + clock; `persist.ts` is file I/O + validation; `server.ts` is HTTP.
- **Shape validation via `isPersistedStore` type guard**: Top-level must be a plain object; each entry must be `{ value: string, ttlMs: number | null }`.
- **Missing file on load = first run (empty store)**: `ENOENT` is the only error code that yields a graceful empty store.
- **`loadStore(file, clock?)` has optional clock parameter**: Needed for tests that use a fake clock.
- **`mkdirSync(dirname(file), { recursive: true })` on both load and save**: Ensures parent directory exists.
- **Shutdown is idempotent**: `shuttingDown` flag prevents double-save.
- **Exit codes**: Save failure → `process.exit(1)`. Success → `process.exit(0)`.
- **No atomic write (temp file + rename)**: Acceptable for a small store.
- **Load test two-phase design (PUTs then GETs)**: Guarantees all GETs return 200 (no 404 noise from phase-boundary races). Still 50 in-flight per phase.
- **Load test uses `createHandler` import, not `KV_PORT`**: The main-module guard doesn't apply to imports, so no env var needed for the in-process server.
- **Load test shared cursor pattern**: `let next = 0; const i = next++` is safe in single-threaded JS (no `await` between read and increment).
- **Load test drains response bodies** (`await res.text()`): Allows keep-alive socket reuse across workers.
- **Load test cleanup**: `server.closeAllConnections()` + `server.close()` + `process.exit(code)` — avoids hang from undici keep-alive sockets.
- **Load test exit code**: 0 on success, 1 if any request returned ≥ 400.
- **ETag is a strong tag (quoted SHA-256 hex)**: Per RFC 7232. No store changes needed — the tag is derived from the value, so it stays correct across restarts.
- **PUT status code kept at 200 (not 201)**: Tests assert 200; preserving existing behavior to avoid breaking tests.
- **`etagMatches` implements weak comparison**: Strips `W/` prefix before comparing, accepts `*` and comma-separated lists. A tag only matches the *current* value, so stale tags fall through to a full 200.
- **304 carries the ETag header**: RFC 7232 §3.2 recommends it; tests assert it.
- **`etagFor` and `etagMatches` exported from server.ts**: Enables unit-testing `etagMatches` directly and reusing `etagFor` in integration tests.
- **`json()` extended with optional `headers` parameter**: `json(res, status, body, headers?)` — merged with `content-type: application/json` in the writeHead call.

## Goal
Build a small in-memory key-value store served over HTTP in TypeScript (using `node:http`), with:
- GET/PUT/DELETE on `/kv/:key`
- Standardized error envelope
- 64 KiB value size limit
- No npm dependencies (stdlib only)
- Tests via `node --test`
- **TTL support**: `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>`, expired keys behave as missing, injectable clock for tests
- **Key listing**: `GET /kv` returns sorted live keys; optional `?prefix=` filter
- **Explicit port configuration**: port read from `KV_PORT` env var; fail at startup if missing or invalid
- **Persistence**: on shutdown (SIGTERM/SIGINT), write store to JSON file specified by `KV_DATA_FILE`; load on startup; expired keys excluded
- **Atomic persistence write**: temp file in same directory + fsync + rename
- **Load test**: in-process benchmark script (`scripts/load.ts`) sending 20,000 requests with 50 in flight
- **ETag / conditional GETs**: `ETag` header on GET/PUT responses; `If-None-Match` → `304 Not Modified` with empty body
- **Compare-and-set (CAS)**: PUT with `If-Match` applies write only when current ETag matches; 412 on failure

## Constraints & Preferences
- **No npm dependencies** — only Node standard library and local imports (stated as a rule by the user)
- TypeScript files run directly by Node ≥ 22 (actually v26.8.2 in this environment)
- `localhost` does NOT resolve in this environment (DNS `EAI_AGAIN`) — use `127.0.0.1` in tests
- Error responses must use the envelope: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`
- Values limited to 64 KiB; larger PUTs get 413
- Clock must be injectable so tests advance time without sleeping
- **No hard-coded port** — the port must come solely from `KV_PORT`; no default, no magic number in code or docs
- **`KV_DATA_FILE` is optional** — unset means in-memory only; no persistence
- PUT status code is **200** (not 201) — preserved from original implementation; tests assert 200

## Key Decisions
- **`fileURLToPath` for main-module check**: `pathToFileURL(import.meta.url)` was wrong. `fileURLToPath` is correct for converting a file URL to a filesystem path.
- **`127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` in tests**: `localhost` doesn't resolve via DNS in this environment (`EAI_AGAIN`).
- **`createHandler(store)` factory**: Allows tests to create their own server on a random port (`listen(0)`) without the main-module guard triggering.
- **`Buffer.byteLength` for size check**: 64 KiB means bytes, not characters.
- **Post-read size check (not streaming)**: Full body is buffered before the check. Acceptable for a small in-memory store.
- **`error()` helper function**: Wraps `json()` to produce the standard `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` envelope.
- **`createStore(clock)` factory pattern**: Chosen over a mutable `setClock()` for cleaner isolation. `node --test` runs each file in a separate process.
- **Lazy expiry (purge-on-read)**: No background sweeper; `get()` and `del()` check `clock() >= expiresAt` and delete on the spot.
- **Expiry boundary uses `>=`**: A key set at time `T` with TTL `S` is expired at exactly `T + S*1000` ms.
- **`del()` returns `false` for expired keys**: "Expired keys behave as if they don't exist."
- **`list()` also purges expired entries**: Consistent with `get()`/`del()` — iterating and lazily removing expired keys before filtering.
- **Exact `/kv` route before per-key regex**: Prevents the regex from accidentally matching; explicit ordering allows 405 semantics specific to the listing endpoint.
- **`KV_PORT` validated at startup only in main-module block**: The check is inside the `process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` guard, so test imports of `createHandler` are unaffected.
- **`KV_PORT` validation covers empty string**: `rawPort === undefined || rawPort === ""` treats both as "missing."
- **`Number()` + `Number.isInteger()` for port validation**: Handles non-numeric strings, floats, out-of-range values.
- **`<port>` placeholder in README and error message**: Avoids introducing any specific number that could be mistaken for a default.
- **Startup tests spawn `node src/server.ts` as child process**: Uses `execFile(process.execPath, [serverPath], { env })` to control the environment precisely.
- **Fixed port 18901 in startup test**: Chosen as an unlikely-to-collide high port; acceptable for a test that kills its child in `finally`.
- **`KV_DATA_FILE` is optional**: Unset = in-memory only. Not required (unlike `KV_PORT`).
- **Persist remaining TTL in ms (relative), not absolute epoch**: Works with injectable fake clock in tests. On load, `expiresAt = clock() + ttlMs`.
- **`serialize()` purges expired entries as a side effect**: Consistent with lazy-expiry semantics.
- **`load()` replaces all contents**: `data.clear()` then re-insert.
- **Separate `src/persist.ts` module**: Clean layering — `store.ts` is pure in-memory + clock; `persist.ts` is file I/O + validation; `server.ts` is HTTP.
- **Shape validation via `isPersistedStore` type guard**: Top-level must be a plain object; each entry must be `{ value: string, ttlMs: number | null }`.
- **Missing file on load = first run (empty store)**: `ENOENT` is the only error code that yields a graceful empty store.
- **`loadStore(file, clock?)` has optional clock parameter**: Needed for tests that use a fake clock.
- **`mkdirSync(dirname(file), { recursive: true })` on both load and save**: Ensures parent directory exists.
- **Shutdown is idempotent**: `shuttingDown` flag prevents double-save.
- **Exit codes**: Save failure → `process.exit(1)`. Success → `process.exit(0)`.
- **Atomic write via temp file + rename**: `${file}.${process.pid}.tmp` in same directory; `fsync` before rename; best-effort `unlink` on failure. Rename within the same filesystem/directory is atomic.
- **Temp file uses `process.pid` (not `randomUUID`)**: Single-writer model; pid is sufficient uniqueness. Avoids importing `crypto`.
- **CAS reuses `etagMatches` helper**: Same weak-comparison logic as `If-None-Match`. `*` requires the resource to exist (per RFC 7232), so a missing key fails even for `*`.
- **CAS checked after size/ttl validation, before `store.set`**: Order: parse ttl → check size → check If-Match → write.

content.text:
# ts-kv A tiny in-memory key-value store served over HTTP, written in TypeScript and run directly by Node (>= 22, which executes `.ts` files natively). **Constraint: no npm dependencies.** Only the Node standard library and local imports are used. If a feature seems to need a package, use a stdlib equivalent or hand-roll it. ## Run The port is taken from the `KV_PORT` environment variable. The server exits at startup with an error if `KV_PORT` is missing or not a valid port. ```sh KV_PORT= npm start ``` Optionally set `KV_DATA_FILE` to persist the store to a JSON file (see [Persistence](#persistence)): ```sh KV_PORT= KV_DATA_FILE=data/kv.json npm start ``` ### Request logging Every request is logged to stderr, one line per request: ``` METHOD PATH STATUS DURATIONms ``` for example: ``` PUT /kv/a 200 1.23ms GET /kv/missing 404 0.41ms ``` Pass `--quiet` to disable request logging: ```sh KV_PORT= npm start -- --quiet ``` ## Test ```sh npm test # node --test ``` ## API Base path `/kv/:key`, JSON responses. | Method | Path | Success | Errors | |--------|----------|---------|--------| | GET | `/healthz` | `200 {"ok":true,"keys":}` | `405` for non-GET | | GET | `/kv?prefix=

` | `200 {"keys": [...]}` (sorted live keys; optional prefix filter) | `405` for non-GET | | GET | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"key", "value"}` + `ETag` header; `304` (empty body, `ETag` header) when `If-None-Match` matches | `404` key not found | | PUT | `/kv/:key?ttl=` | `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` + `ETag` header (raw body is the value, max 64 KiB) | `400` invalid ttl, `412` If-Match failed, `413` value too large | | DELETE | `/kv/:key` | `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` | `404` key not found | All error responses use the envelope: ```json {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}} ``` Codes: `not_found` (unknown path), `key_not_found`, `value_too_large`, `method_not_allowed` (405), `invalid_ttl` (400), `precondition_failed` (412). ### TTL `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=` stores the key with a time-to-live. The clock is injected into the store (`createStore(clock)`) so tests advance time without sleeping. Expired keys behave exactly as missing: `GET` and `DELETE` return `404 key_not_found`. `ttl` must be a positive number of seconds. ### ETags `GET` and `PUT` responses carry an `ETag`: a strong tag — the quoted SHA-256 hex digest of the value (RFC 7232). Send `If-None-Match` with a previously returned tag and the server answers `304 Not Modified` with an empty body instead of the value; the tag is still sent on the 304. Weak (`W/`) tags, `*`, and comma-separated lists are all accepted (weak comparison). The tag changes whenever the value changes, so a stale tag simply gets a full `200` again. **Compare-and-set:** a `PUT` with an `If-Match` header is applied only if the current value's ETag matches (same weak-comparison rules: `W/` tags, `*`, comma-separated lists). On failure the store is unchanged and the response is `412` with the standard error envelope (`precondition_failed`). A missing key fails the precondition too, including for `If-Match: *` — so the usual CAS loop is: `GET` to learn the current ETag, `PUT` with that `If-Match`, and on `412` re-read and retry. ## Persistence When `KV_DATA_FILE` is set, the store is loaded from that JSON file on startup and snapshotted back to it when the process receives `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`. Without it, the store is purely in-memory. - **First run:** if the file does not exist, the store starts empty (the file is created on the first shutdown snapshot; parent directories are created as needed). - **Corrupt file:** a file that is not valid JSON or does not have the snapshot shape causes startup to fail with a clear error (exit 1). - **Expired keys are not written:** the snapshot contains live entries only. Keys with a remaining TTL keep it, recorded as `ttlMs` relative to the snapshot time, so a restarted server preserves the original expiry. - **Atomic snapshot:** the write goes to a temp file in the same directory, is fsynced, and is then renamed over the data file — a crash mid-write never leaves a truncated or corrupt data file (at worst a stale temp file, which the next save overwrites). Snapshot format: ```json { "greeting": { "value": "hi", "ttlMs": null }, "session:abc": { "value": "...", "ttlMs": 41250 } } ```

## Goal
Build a small in-memory key-value store served over HTTP in TypeScript (using `node:http`), with:
- GET/PUT/DELETE on `/kv/:key`
- Standardized error envelope
- 64 KiB value size limit
- No npm dependencies (stdlib only)
- Tests via `node --test`
- **TTL support**: `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>`, expired keys behave as missing, injectable clock for tests
- **Key listing**: `GET /kv` returns sorted live keys; optional `?prefix=` filter
- **Explicit port configuration**: port read from `KV_PORT` env var; fail at startup if missing or invalid
- **Persistence**: on shutdown (SIGTERM/SIGINT), write store to JSON file specified by `KV_DATA_FILE`; load on startup; expired keys excluded
- **Atomic persistence write**: temp file in same directory + fsync + rename
- **Load test**: in-process benchmark script (`scripts/load.ts`) sending 20,000 requests with 50 in flight
- **ETag / conditional GETs**: `ETag` header on GET/PUT responses; `If-None-Match` → `304 Not Modified` with empty body
- **Compare-and-set (CAS)**: PUT with `If-Match` applies write only when current ETag matches; 412 on failure
- **Health check**: `GET /healthz` returns `{"ok": true, "keys": <live count>}`; non-GET → 405

## Constraints & Preferences
- **No npm dependencies** — only Node standard library and local imports (stated as a rule by the user)
- TypeScript files run directly by Node ≥ 22 (actually v26.8.2 in this environment)
- `localhost` does NOT resolve in this environment (DNS `EAI_AGAIN`) — use `127.0.0.1` in tests
- Error responses must use the envelope: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`
- Values limited to 64 KiB; larger PUTs get 413
- Clock must be injectable so tests advance time without sleeping
- **No hard-coded port** — the port must come solely from `KV_PORT`; no default, no magic number in code or docs

## Key Decisions
- **`fileURLToPath` for main-module check**: `pathToFileURL(import.meta.url)` was wrong. `fileURLToPath` is correct for converting a file URL to a filesystem path.
- **`127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` in tests**: `localhost` doesn't resolve via DNS in this environment (`EAI_AGAIN`).
- **`createHandler(store)` factory**: Allows tests to create their own server on a random port (`listen(0)`) without the main-module guard triggering.
- **`Buffer.byteLength` for size check**: 64 KiB means bytes, not characters.
- **Post-read size check (not streaming)**: Full body is buffered before the check. Acceptable for a small in-memory store.
- **`error()` helper function**: Wraps `json()` to produce the standard `{"error": {"code", "message"}}` envelope.
- **`createStore(clock)` factory pattern**: Chosen over a mutable `setClock()` for cleaner isolation. `node --test` runs each file in a separate process.
- **Lazy expiry (purge-on-read)**: No background sweeper; `get()` and `del()` check `clock() >= expiresAt` and delete on the spot.
- **Expiry boundary uses `>=`**: A key set at time `T` with TTL `S` is expired at exactly `T + S*1000` ms.
- **`del()` returns `false` for expired keys**: "Expired keys behave as if they don't exist."
- **`list()` also purges expired entries**: Consistent with `get()`/`del()` — iterating and lazily removing expired keys before filtering.
- **Exact `/kv` route before per-key regex**: Prevents the regex from accidentally matching; explicit ordering allows 405 semantics specific to the listing endpoint.
- **`KV_PORT` validated at startup only in main-module block**: The check is inside the `process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` guard, so test imports of `createHandler` are unaffected.
- **`KV_PORT` validation covers empty string**: `rawPort === undefined || rawPort === ""` treats both as "missing."
- **`Number()` + `Number.isInteger()` for port validation**: Handles non-numeric strings, floats, out-of-range values.
- **`<port>` placeholder in README and error message**: Avoids introducing any specific number that could be mistaken for a default.
- **Startup tests spawn `node src/server.ts` as child process**: Uses `execFile(process.execPath, [serverPath], { env })` to control the environment precisely.
- **Fixed port 18901 in startup test**: Chosen as an unlikely-to-collide high port; acceptable for a test that kills its child in `finally`.
- **`KV_DATA_FILE` is optional**: Unset = in-memory only. Not required (unlike `KV_PORT`).
- **Persist remaining TTL in ms (relative), not absolute epoch**: Works with injectable fake clock in tests. On load, `expiresAt = clock() + ttlMs`.
- **`serialize()` purges expired entries as a side effect**: Consistent with lazy-expiry semantics.
- **`load()` replaces all contents**: `data.clear()` then re-insert.
- **Separate `src/persist.ts` module**: Clean layering — `store.ts` is pure in-memory + clock; `persist.ts` is file I/O + validation; `server.ts` is HTTP.
- **Shape validation via `isPersistedStore` type guard**: Top-level must be a plain object; each entry must be `{ value: string, ttlMs: number | null }`.
- **Missing file on load = first run (empty store)**: `ENOENT` is the only error code that yields a graceful empty store.
- **`loadStore(file, clock?)` has optional clock parameter**: Needed for tests that use a fake clock.
- **`mkdirSync(dirname(file), { recursive: true })` on both load and save**: Ensures parent directory exists.
- **Shutdown is idempotent**: `shuttingDown` flag prevents double-save.
- **Exit codes**: Save failure → `process.exit(1)`. Success → `process.exit(0)`.
- **Atomic write via temp file + rename**: `${file}.${process.pid}.tmp` in same directory; `fsync` before rename; best-effort `unlink` on failure. Rename within the same filesystem/directory is atomic.
- **Temp file uses `process.pid` (not `randomUUID`)**: Single-writer model; pid is sufficient uniqueness. Avoids importing `crypto`.
- **CAS reuses `etagMatches` helper**: Same weak-comparison logic as `If-None-Match`. `*` requires the resource to exist (per RFC 7232), so a missing key fails even for `*`.
- **CAS checked after size/ttl validation, before `store.set`**: Order: parse ttl → check size → check If-Match → write.
- **`loadStore` returns a store object, not a plain record**: Tests must assert on `s.list()` / `s.get()` rather than deep-equaling against a record.
- **`/healthz` count via `store.list().length`**: Since `list()` already purges expired entries as a side effect, the count is automatically correct without any separate "live key count" method. Avoids adding API surface to the store.
- **`/healthz` placed before `/kv` in route matching**: Same pattern as `/kv` listing — exact path check before the per-key regex, ensuring no accidental match.
- **`/healthz` tests use delta assertions**: Because `test/server.test.ts` shares a single store across all tests, absolute count assertions would be brittle. Tests record a baseline count, PUT/DELETE dedicated keys (h1/h2/h3), and assert relative changes.
- **Port history**: Started as `process.env.PORT ?? 3000` (commit `29f4d1a`), changed to hard-coded `8090` (commit `89c638c`), then replaced with required `KV_PORT` env var (commit `e9dcd04`).

# ts-kv

A small in-memory key-value store served over HTTP, written in TypeScript
and run directly by Node (>= 22, which executes `.ts` files natively).

**Constraint: no npm dependencies.** Only the Node standard library and
local imports are used. If a feature seems to need a package, use a stdlib
equivalent or hand-roll it.

## Run

```sh
KV_PORT=<port> npm start
```

The port comes solely from `KV_PORT` — the server exits at startup with a
clear error if it is missing, empty, or not an integer between 1 and 65535.

Every request is logged to stderr, one line per request:

```
METHOD PATH STATUS DURATIONms
PUT /kv/a 200 1.23ms
GET /kv/missing 404 0.41ms
```

Pass `--quiet` to disable request logging:

```sh
KV_PORT=<port> npm start -- --quiet
```

## Environment variables

| Variable        | Required | Meaning |
|-----------------|----------|---------|
| `KV_PORT`       | yes      | Port to listen on. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535. Missing, empty, or invalid → clear error and exit 1. |
| `KV_DATA_FILE`  | no       | Path of a JSON snapshot file. When set, the store is loaded from it at startup and written back (atomically) on `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`. When unset, the store is purely in-memory. See [Persistence](#persistence). |

## Endpoints

All responses are JSON. Error responses always use the envelope

```json
{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}
```

Values are limited to **64 KiB** (`Buffer.byteLength`); a larger `PUT` gets
`413 value_too_large`. In the examples below, set:

```sh
BASE=http://127.0.0.1:$KV_PORT
```

### GET /healthz

Liveness probe: `200 {"ok":true,"keys":<live count>}` where the count
excludes keys whose TTL has expired. Non-GET → `405`.

```sh
curl -s "$BASE/healthz"
# {"ok":true,"keys":2}

curl -si -X POST "$BASE/healthz"
# HTTP/1.1 405 ...
# {"error":{"code":"method_not_allowed","message":"method not allowed"}}
```

### PUT /kv/:key

Store a value. The raw request body is the value (any bytes, up to 64 KiB).
Response: `200 {"ok":true,"key"}` plus an `ETag` header for the new value.

| Query / Header | Effect |
|---|---|
| `?ttl=<seconds>` | Key expires after the given positive number of seconds; see [TTL](#ttl). Invalid → `400 invalid_ttl`. |
| `If-Match: <etag>` | Compare-and-set: the write is applied only if the current value's ETag matches; otherwise `412 precondition_failed` and the store is unchanged. See [ETags](#etags--compare-and-set). |

```sh
curl -si -X PUT --data 'hello world' "$BASE/kv/greeting"
# HTTP/1.1 200 ...
# etag: "2cf24dba..."
# {"ok":true,"key":"greeting"}
```

#### With a TTL

```sh
curl -s -X PUT --data 'temporary' "$BASE/kv/session:abc?ttl=30"
# {"ok":true,"key":"session:abc"}
```

#### Compare-and-set

Learn the current tag (from any `GET`/`PUT`), then guard the write with it:

```sh
etag=$(curl -sD - -o /dev/null "$BASE/kv/greeting" | tr -d '\r' | awk -F': ' '/^etag/{print $2}')

curl -s -X PUT -H "If-Match: $etag" --data 'hello v2' "$BASE/kv/greeting"
# {"ok":true,"key":"greeting"}          # write applied

curl -si -X PUT -H 'If-Match: "stale"' --data 'hello v3' "$BASE/kv/greeting"
# HTTP/1.1 412 ...
# {"error":{"code":"precondition_failed","message":"if-match does not match the current etag"}}
# value is still 'hello v2'
```

A missing key fails the precondition too (including `If-Match: *`), so the
usual CAS loop is: `GET` → `PUT If-Match` → on `412` re-read and retry.

### GET /kv/:key

`200 {"key","value"}` plus an `ETag` header. `404 key_not_found` if absent
or expired.

```sh
curl -si "$BASE/kv/greeting"
# HTTP/1.1 200 ...
# etag: "..."
# {"key":"greeting","value":"hello v2"}

curl -s "$BASE/kv/ghost"
# {"error":{"code":"key_not_found","message":"key not found"}}
```

#### Conditional GET

Send a previously returned tag in `If-None-Match`; on a match the server
answers `304 Not Modified` with an empty body (tag resent) instead of the
value:

```sh
curl -si -H "If-None-Match: $etag" "$BASE/kv/greeting"
# HTTP/1.1 304 ...
# etag: "..."
# (empty body)
```

Weak (`W/`) tags, `*`, and comma-separated lists are accepted (weak
comparison). A stale tag simply gets a full `200` again.

### DELETE /kv/:key

`200 {"ok":true,"key"}`. `404 key_not_found` if absent or expired.

```sh
curl -s -X DELETE "$BASE/kv/greeting"
# {"ok":true,"key":"greeting"}

curl -s -X DELETE "$BASE/kv/greeting"
# {"error":{"code":"key_not_found","message":"key not found"}}
```

### GET /kv

List live keys, sorted; expired keys are omitted. Optional `?prefix=`
filters to keys starting with the prefix. Non-GET → `405`.

```sh
curl -s "$BASE/kv"
# {"keys":["greeting","session:abc"]}

curl -s "$BASE/kv?prefix=session:"
# {"keys":["session:abc"]}

curl -si -X PUT --data x "$BASE/kv"
# HTTP/1.1 405 ...
# {"error":{"code":"method_not_allowed","message":"method not allowed"}}
```

### Error codes

| Code | Status | When |
|---|---|---|
| `not_found` | 404 | Unknown path |
| `key_not_found` | 404 | Key absent or expired (GET/DELETE `/kv/:key`) |
| `method_not_allowed` | 405 | Wrong method for the path |
| `value_too_large` | 413 | PUT body exceeds 64 KiB |
| `invalid_ttl` | 400 | `ttl` is not a positive number of seconds |
| `precondition_failed` | 412 | PUT `If-Match` does not match (key may be missing) |

## TTL

`PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>` stores the key with a time-to-live; `ttl` must
be a positive number of seconds. Expired keys behave exactly as missing:
`GET`/`DELETE` return `404`, `GET /kv` and `/healthz` omit them. The clock is
injected into the store (`createStore(clock)`) so tests advance time without
sleeping.

## ETags / compare-and-set

`GET` and `PUT` responses carry an `ETag`: a strong tag — the quoted
SHA-256 hex digest of the value (RFC 7232). `If-None-Match` → `304`;
`If-Match` on `PUT` → CAS with `412` on mismatch. Weak (`W/`) tags, `*`,
and comma-separated lists are accepted (weak comparison). The tag changes
whenever the value changes, so a stale tag simply gets a full `200` again.

## Persistence

When `KV_DATA_FILE` is set, the store is loaded from that JSON file on
startup and snapshotted back to it when the process receives `SIGINT` or
`SIGTERM`. Without it, the store is purely in-memory.

- **First run:** ... (keep as-is)
- **Corrupt file:** ...
- **Expired keys are not written:** ...
- **Atomic snapshot:** ...

Snapshot format: (keep the json)

## Test / load

```sh
npm test        # node --test, 55 tests
npm run load    # in-process benchmark: 20,000 requests, 50 in flight
```
```

Wait — a small point about the GET /kv listing example: `?prefix=session:` — inside double quotes, `session:` is fine.

Another point: `curl -sD - -o /dev/null "$BASE/kv/greeting" | tr -d '\r' | awk -F': ' '/^etag/{print $2}'` — header line: `etag: "2cf2..."`. With -F': ', $1="etag", $2='"2cf2..."'. Good.

One concern: does the awk pattern `'/^etag/'` match? After tr -d '\r', the line is `etag: "..."`. Yes.

Also a note about curl HEAD: I don't use -I anywhere, good.

PUT's `--data 'hello world'` sends `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` — the server ignores content type and treats the raw body as the value. Fine.

Also, the example flow: in the GET /kv/:key section I use `$etag`, which is defined in the PUT/CAS section — the sections are in the order PUT before GET, so this works sequentially. Good, my ordering is: healthz → PUT → GET → DELETE → listing. In the GET section I reference $etag (defined in the CAS subsection of PUT).

Hmm, wait, in my draft above I had the order: healthz, PUT (with TTL + CAS), GET (with conditional), DELETE, listing. Yes, $etag is defined before use.

About the 405 example on PUT /kv in the listing section: `curl -si -X PUT --data x "$BASE/kv"` — 405 method_not_allowed. Good.

Keep the test count accurate: currently 55. Rather than hardcoding 55... the original README said `npm test # node --test`. To avoid staleness, I'll leave it as `# node --test` without a count.

Length: it'll be long, but the user explicitly asked for endpoints + environment variables + curl for each endpoint. Fine.

Let me also double-check the exact response format so the examples are accurate:
- healthz: `{"ok":true,"keys":2}` ✓
- PUT: `{"ok":true,"key":"greeting"}` ✓
- GET: `{"key":"greeting","value":"hello v2"}` ✓
- DELETE: `{"ok":true,"key":"greeting"}` ✓
- listing: `{"keys":[...]}` ✓
- Errors: key_not_found message "key not found" ✓; not_found "not found"; method_not_allowed "method not allowed" ✓; value_too_large "value exceeds 64 kib limit" ✓; invalid_ttl "ttl must be a positive number of seconds" ✓; precondition_failed "if-match does not match the current etag" ✓

Status lines: node sends `HTTP/1.1 200` — in the curl -si output it shows as `HTTP/1.1 200`. I'll write `HTTP/1.1 200 ...` — the ellipsis hides the reason phrase. Fine.

Now, should I preserve the "API" table? The endpoint sections replace it. The table was a nice summary, but the user asked for per-endpoint curl examples — a full rewrite is justified. Keep the envelope + error code table.

Let me write the file. Then verify the README examples actually work against a live server (good practice): run the example sequence. I'll do a quick live check of a few of the trickier ones (etag extraction + CAS + conditional GET) — mostly already verified. Just in case, let me verify the awk extraction pipeline.

### `GET /kv`

List live keys, sorted; expired keys are omitted. Optional `?prefix=`
filters to keys starting with the prefix. Non-GET → `405`.

```sh
curl -s "$BASE/kv"
# {"keys":["greeting","session:abc"]}

curl -s "$BASE/kv?prefix=session:"
# {"keys":["session:abc"]}

curl -si -X PUT --data x "$BASE/kv"
# HTTP/1.1 405
# {"error":{"code":"method_not_allowed","message":"method not allowed"}}
```

### Error codes

| Code                  | Status | When |
|-----------------------|--------|------|
| `not_found`           | 404    | Unknown path |
| `key_not_found`       | 404    | Key absent or expired (`GET`/`DELETE /kv/:key`) |
| `method_not_allowed`  | 405    | Wrong method for the path |
| `value_too_large`     | 413    | `PUT` body exceeds 64 KiB |
| `invalid_ttl`         | 400    | `ttl` is not a positive number of seconds |
| `precondition_failed` | 412    | `PUT` `If-Match` does not match (a missing key fails too) |

## TTL

`PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>` stores the key with a time-to-live; `ttl` must
be a positive number of seconds. Expired keys behave exactly as missing:
`GET`/`DELETE` return `404 key_not_found`, `GET /kv` and `/healthz` omit
them, and they are dropped from snapshots. The clock is injected into the
store (`createStore(clock)`) so tests advance time without sleeping.

## ETags / compare-and-set

`GET` and `PUT` responses carry an `ETag`: a strong tag — the quoted
SHA-256 hex digest of the value (RFC 7232). The tag changes whenever the
value changes.

- `If-None-Match` on `GET` → `304 Not Modified` (empty body) on a match.
- `If-Match` on `PUT` → compare-and-set; `412 precondition_failed` and an
  unchanged store on a mismatch. A missing key fails the precondition,
  including for `If-Match: *`.

Weak (`W/`) tags, `*`, and comma-separated lists are accepted everywhere (weak
comparison).

## Persistence

When `KV_DATA_FILE` is set, the store is loaded from that JSON file on
startup and snapshotted back to it when the process receives `SIGINT` or
`SIGTERM`. Without it, the store is purely in-memory.

- **First run:** if the file does not exist, the store starts empty (the
  file is created on the first shutdown snapshot; parent directories are
  created as needed).
- **Corrupt file:** a file that is not valid JSON or does not have the
  snapshot shape causes startup to fail with a clear error (exit 1).
- **Expired keys are not written:** the snapshot contains live entries only.
  Keys with a remaining TTL keep it, recorded as `ttlMs` relative to the
  snapshot time, so a restarted server preserves the original expiry.
- **Atomic snapshot:** the write goes to a temp file in the same directory,
  is fsynced, and is then renamed over the data file — a crash mid-write
  never leaves a truncated or corrupt data file (at worst a stale temp file,
  which the next save overwrites).

Snapshot format:

```json
{
  "greeting": { "value": "hi", "ttlMs": null },
  "session:abc": { "value": "...", "ttlMs": 41250 }
}
```

## Test / load

```sh
npm test        # node --test
npm run load    # in-process benchmark: 20,000 requests, 50 in flight
```

summary:
## Goal
Build a small in-memory key-value store served over HTTP in TypeScript (using `node:http`), with:
- GET/PUT/DELETE on `/kv/:key`
- Standardized error envelope
- 64 KiB value size limit
- No npm dependencies (stdlib only)
- Tests via `node --test`
- **TTL support**: `PUT /kv/:key?ttl=<seconds>`, expired keys behave as missing, injectable clock for tests
- **Key listing**: `GET /kv` returns sorted live keys; optional `?prefix=` filter
- **Explicit port configuration**: port read from `KV_PORT` env var; fail at startup if missing or invalid
- **Persistence**: on shutdown (SIGTERM/SIGINT), write store to JSON file specified by `KV_DATA_FILE`; load on startup; expired keys excluded
- **Atomic persistence write**: temp file in same directory + fsync + rename
- **Load test**: in-process benchmark script (`scripts/load.ts`) sending 20,000 requests with 50 in flight
- **ETag / conditional GETs**: `ETag` header on GET/PUT responses; `If-None-Match` → `304 Not Modified` with empty body
- **Compare-and-set (CAS)**: PUT with `If-Match` applies write only when current ETag matches; 412 on failure
- **Health check**: `GET /healthz` returns `{"ok": true, "keys": <live count>}`; non-GET → 405
- **Request logging**: every request logged to stderr as `METHOD PATH STATUS DURATIONms`; `--quiet` flag disables logging

## Constraints & Preferences
- **No npm dependencies** — only Node standard library and local imports (stated as a rule by the user)
- TypeScript files run directly by Node ≥ 22 (actually v26.8.2 in this environment)
